resources.string: An open agent that uses your phone for you. Ask once, then get on with your day.
About 3 minutes. Most steps can be skipped.

Tasks run on a separate virtual screen, so your phone stays free. Orbit tells you when it’s done or needs you.
Orbit is open source and has no servers of its own.
All of the code is public. No account, no ads, no tracking.
Your chats, memory, files and task history. API keys are encrypted with the phone’s keystore.
What you ask, plus the screen or page Orbit is working on. It goes straight to the provider you pick next, not through any Orbit server.
Orbit thinks with a model you bring. You can change it any time in Settings.
Sign in with Google. No API key. Needs about 1.2 GB and Wi-Fi to set up.
Continue with ChatGPT Plus or Pro. No API key.
Paste your API key. It is stored encrypted on this phone.
Orbit listed the models and ran a test tool call. Both worked.
A main model is set. Orbit is ready to think.
Orbit taps and types through Android’s own wireless debugging. Pair once, right here. No computer, no root.
Chat, web and files work without it.
Orbit can now use your apps on a separate virtual screen while you keep using your phone.
Orbit asks for each one the first time it matters. Allow them now if you’d rather not be interrupted later.
To tell you when a task is done or needs you.
A small capsule shows what Orbit is doing while you’re in other apps. It needs no extra permission.
So scheduled tasks start on time. Asked when you first schedule one.
The microphone is asked the first time you hold to talk. You can change all of these in Android settings.
Two optional extras. Both can wait.
Used in greetings. Kept on this phone.
Send Orbit a task by messaging yourself, from anywhere. Orbit reads only the chats you pick.
